summary: International conference following the First Moroccan Crisis; established the State Bank of Morocco and European supervision of customs and police while formally affirming Moroccan sovereignty.
mainDispute: Whether it was a genuine multilateral guarantee or a managed transfer of Morocco to France with German consent purchased later.

event: Treaty of Fez and the April 1912 rising
summary: Treaty of 30 March 1912 establishing the French protectorate, signed by Abdelhafid and Regnault; the Fez rising of 17 April 1912 on its disclosure; and the Franco-Spanish treaty of 27 November 1912 partitioning the country.
mainDispute: Whether the Arabic and French texts differ in substance — the foundation of the Moroccan legal argument that the protectorate was void. Casualties in the April rising. Whether the rising was a soldiers' mutiny over pay or a political insurrection.

event: Deposition, exile and return of Mohammed V
summary: The French Residency and a coalition of pashas and qaids led by El Glaoui deposed the sultan and installed Ben Arafa; two years of resistance forced his return and led directly to independence.
mainDispute: Who decided — Paris, the Residency, or El Glaoui. Casualty figures in the resistance of 1953-55. Whether the Army of Liberation or the negotiations produced independence.

location: Casablanca (Dar el-Beida) and the Chaouia plain
summary: Killing of nine European port workers on 30 July 1907 followed by French naval bombardment 5-7 August, landing, sack of the city, and the occupation of the Chaouia — the first permanent French military presence in Atlantic Morocco.
mainDispute: The death toll, where estimates range from 600 to well over 3,000. Whether the bombardment was a proportionate protection of nationals or a pre-planned seizure. Responsibility for the looting.

location: Eastern Rif; Melilla hinterland; from 1925 the Ouergha valley in the French zone
summary: Spanish military collapse in the eastern Rif in July-August 1921, followed by five years of war against the Rif Republic ending with Abd el-Krim's surrender to France at Targuist, 26 May 1926.
mainDispute: Total Spanish dead (7,875 to 13,363). Silvestre's manner of death. Alfonso XIII's alleged encouragement of the advance. Whether Monte Arruit was a massacre after surrender on terms or a fight that continued. The scale of Spanish chemical weapons use.

location: Rabat; reaction in Salé, Fez and across the French zone
summary: Dahir of 16 May 1930 placing Tamazight-speaking tribes under customary-law tribunals with serious crime before French courts; triggered the Ya Latif campaign and the emergence of mass Moroccan nationalism.
mainDispute: Whether it was a deliberate de-Islamisation plot or an extension of existing legislation that was received as one. Whether Mohammed V signed freely.

summary: Moroccan army under the sultan's son Sidi Mohammed destroyed by Bugeaud's French force; led to the Treaty of Tangier and the Lalla Maghnia border convention.
mainDispute: Moroccan troop numbers and casualties, which French accounts inflate. Whether the defeat was as total as French reporting claimed.

summary: Convened at Hassan I's request to limit consular protection; instead codified it and granted foreigners the right to own land in Morocco.
mainDispute: How many protected persons there actually were, and what share of taxable wealth they removed from the Makhzen.

location: El Herri (El Hri, Lehri), c. 15 km south of Khénifra, Middle Atlas
summary: A French column of 1,230 men under Lt-Col Laverdure raided Mouha ou Hammou Zayani's camp without orders, then was destroyed during its withdrawal. 623 French and colonial troops killed — France's heaviest single defeat in Morocco.
mainDispute: Zaian casualties (the French battlefield count of 182 is a French count). Whether responsibility lies with Laverdure's indiscipline (the official French line) or with Lyautey's wartime force posture. Whether the raid's aim was Hammou himself or his camp.

event: Hispano-Moroccan War and the Treaty of Wad Ras
summary: Spanish invasion and capture of Tetouan; the resulting indemnity mortgaged Moroccan customs revenue for decades.
mainDispute: The real burden of the indemnity as a share of state revenue. Whether Britain brokered the terms to protect its own commercial position.
